Introduction

Ohio’s Non-Medical Home Health Services License allows providers to offer personal care and homemaker services. The OH Department of Health — Bureau of Regulatory Operations oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Ohio’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Ohio’s Regulations

OH DOH licenses non-medical home health services under Ohio Administrative Code. Requirements include licensing, background checks via BCI&I, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and chore services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the OH Secretary of State, apply for non-medical home health services license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Ohio benchmarks: Private pay rates $20-$28/hour, Medicaid waiver rates $15-$22/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and quality monitoring systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Ohio requires BCI&I background checks and training for all direct care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting OH DOH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati, and other Ohio communities.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and compliance with regulatory requirements.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between medical and non-medical home health? Non-medical covers personal care and homemaker services without nursing or therapy.
